 Opinion: UFC 333 could reshape featherweight, bantamweight GOAT debates
 Dayne Fox Oct 23, 2026 
 With
two UFC 333 title fights on tap, Alexander Volkanovski, Petr Yan
and Merab Dvalishvili have more than championship gold at stake.
Their places in MMA history could be on the line. | 📷:
UFC/Paramount 
 Editor’s note: The views and opinions expressed below are those
of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of
Sherdog.com, its affiliates and sponsors or its parent company,
Evolve Media. 
 * * * 
For all the complaints about 
Ultimate Fighting Championship cards since the Paramount deal
took effect, there will be no grumbling about 
UFC 333 from me. With two title fights at the top, at least two
other bouts likely to shape their divisions’ championship pictures
over the next year and several prospects who could eventually join
those conversations, there’s plenty to be excited about.
 Advertisement 
However, even with the two championship bouts commanding most of
the attention, I don’t believe their historical stakes are
receiving enough weight. Those implications aren’t being ignored,
but they feel like an afterthought in the UFC’s promotion. Perhaps
that’s because the fighters whose legacies are at stake don’t
command attention quite like Max
Holloway or Sean
O'Malley . Whatever the reason, these shouldn’t be treated as
routine title fights. Both could strengthen a winner’s claim to
being his division’s greatest of all time.
 Alexander Volkanovski's UFC 333 title defense could strengthen
his featherweight GOAT case
Despite headlining, the featherweight contest feels like the
smaller of the two. There are several reasons for that. Movsar
Evloev has finally received a title opportunity after 10 UFC
victories, all by decision. His style has attracted criticism, and
the wait has fueled debate about how much entertainment value
influences matchmaking. Meanwhile, reigning champion Alexander
Volkanovski feels more like a placeholder than the division’s
unquestioned leader. His stretch of three losses in four
appearances wasn’t that long ago, and two uneventful fights with
 Diego
Lopes have followed.
Before I undermine my argument any further, two of those three
losses came at lightweight against Islam
Makhachev . The third was against Ilia
Topuria , who later became lightweight champion. That
featherweight defeat cost Volkanovski his belt and remains the main
reason his current reign feels incomplete. It’s harder to get
excited about a champion’s return to the throne when he didn’t
reclaim it from the man who dethroned him.
Still, Volkanovski has lost only once at 145 pounds. That’s fewer
featherweight defeats than either Holloway or Jose Aldo , the
other leading candidates for the division’s greatest fighter.
Topuria holds a victory over him, but he lacks Volkanovski’s
sustained record against elite featherweights. Conor
McGregor ’s victory over Aldo doesn’t automatically place him
above the Brazilian in the division’s historical hierarchy. Aldo’s
extended success carries more weight. The same principle benefits
Volkanovski.
 Volkanovski could surpass Jose Aldo's UFC featherweight
title-fight record
If Volkanovski beats the undefeated Evloev at 38, his case becomes
difficult to dismiss. He would reach nine UFC featherweight
title-fight victories, breaking his tie with Aldo, at an age when
most fighters in the division have declined. Add three victories
over Holloway, and the argument becomes stronger still.
 Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili 3 could reshape the bantamweight
GOAT debate
Bantamweight’s historical hierarchy could also shift, though the
stakes are more evenly distributed between Petr Yan and
 Merab
Dvalishvili . Evloev would still have much to prove after
winning the championship. Yan and Dvalishvili have already
assembled substantial legacies. Their trilogy winner could emerge
with a credible claim to the division’s top historical spot.
That may sound ambitious. Dvalishvili won 14 consecutive fights,
including three successful title defenses. Yan is in his second
reign as undisputed bantamweight champion but has yet to make a
successful defense. He also endured a stretch of four losses in
five appearances. A closer look, however, reveals more nuance than
those results alone suggest.
Yan first lost his championship to Aljamain
Sterling by disqualification after landing an illegal knee to
his grounded opponent. Yan had taken control before that costly
mistake, but the foul and resulting loss were his responsibility.
After beating Cory
Sandhagen for the interim title, he lost a split decision to
Sterling in their rematch. That result was debated, though a
majority of the media scores compiled by MMA Decisions favored
Sterling. Yan’s subsequent split-decision loss to O’Malley drew
considerably broader disagreement: Only one of the 26 media scorers
listed by MMA Decisions favored O’Malley.
Yan’s case would be less clear-cut than Dvalishvili’s even with
another victory. Still, winning their trilogy would give him a
significant argument, particularly for those who believe his record
understates his performances. Avenging the O’Malley defeat would
strengthen it further. Given O’Malley’s popularity and the UFC’s
apparent enthusiasm for promoting him, that rematch seems a
plausible next step if Yan retains the belt.
 Merab Dvalishvili could tie T.J. Dillashaw's UFC bantamweight
title-fight record
Beating Dvalishvili again won’t be easy. Yan’s performance in their
rematch was excellent, but Dvalishvili was attempting an
unprecedented fourth successful UFC title defense in a calendar
year. It’s reasonable to wonder whether that schedule affected him,
though we can’t know how much. After more than 10 months between
appearances, he could return refreshed. A victory would give him
five UFC bantamweight title-fight wins, tying T.J.
Dillashaw ’s divisional record. Perhaps I shouldn’t minimize
Evloev’s stakes, either. He remains undefeated and could begin a
lengthy championship reign. A loss would leave his next opportunity
uncertain, particularly given how long he waited for this one. An
immediate rematch would likely require an unusually compelling
first encounter, but predicting that he would never receive another
title shot goes too far. He isn’t yet a central figure in the
division’s greatest-of-all-time debate. He could become one over
the next few years, and UFC 333 offers the starting point. For the
other three title fighters, Saturday could provide some of the
strongest evidence yet for their places in history.
